messages:
incident-bot: [Page] High-sev: unexpected routing of hosted tenants into dedicated pools causing increased latency and partial tenant exposure risk. Pager: maya (eng-oncall). PD: INC-8942. Links: https://pagerduty.com/INC-8942, internal runbook: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/routing-fallback

pagerduty-bot: ACK recorded, escalation to SRE oncall. Paging maya.

maya (eng-oncall): on it. joining via call now. seeing alerts for tenant:tierA and tenant:tierB. both show 5xxs + elevated p99.

alex (sre): I see a spike in requests routed from hosted -> dedicated pool-delta-2 with header mismatch. Logs show header X-tenant-id was rewritten to tenant:different-namespace for ~20k requests starting 1702504200.

carla (runtime): hmm, that sounds like the fallback policy mixin we deployed last night. There was a change to policy "capacity-tier-fallthrough" to allow cross-pool spillover during bursts.

linh (platform): I rolled that change as a patch at 1702499000 to allow soft-burst to dedicated, but I scoped it by tag. Maybe the tag selector didn't match exactly.

maya (eng-oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable fallthrough policy 2) rebind affected tenants to hosted ONLY 3) scale hosted pool for immediate headroom. who can flip the policy?

ops-automation: available ops command: 
```
redwoodctl policies update capacity-tier-fallthrough --enabled=false --env prod
```

alex (sre): running redwoodctl to disable now (I'll echo commands).

alex (sre): `redwoodctl policies update capacity-tier-fallthrough --enabled=false --env prod`

ops-automation: policy update accepted, propagating. should take ~15s to reach routing-layer.

carla (runtime): I'm also pushing a targeted rule to pin tenant:tierA and tenant:tierB to hosted pools to avoid any residual leakage: 
```
redwoodctl routes bind --tenant tierA --pool hosted-pool-1 --force
redwoodctl routes bind --tenant tierB --pool hosted-pool-1 --force
```

maya (eng-oncall): executing binds now.

maya (eng-oncall): binds complete. monitoring.

sam (support): Customer-impact note: support queue has 3 open tickets for slow responses and 1 outage report from acct-omega. Marking impacted customers: acct-omega, acct-alpha, acct-beta. Preparing comms draft.

alex (sre): telemetry: p99 latency for tenant:tierA went from 120ms -> 2.3s at peak, errors 5xx rose to 12%. After policy toggle, p99 dropping to 200ms and errors trending down.

carla (runtime): I'm seeing some leftover KV-cache entries in the routing cache that still map a handful of prefixes to dedicated. Purging now: 
```
redis-cli -h routing-cache del routing:tenant:tierA*
```

ops-automation: cache purge triggered and confirmed.

maya (eng-oncall): good. taking ownership for next 30 mins to watch for regression. alex, can you prepare a short post-incident note w/ root cause hypothesis? I'll handle customer outreach and severity.

alex (sre): yes. preliminary RCA: regression introduced by capacity-tier-fallthrough policy where tag selector used `team:owned` but runtime tags were `team=owned` (equals vs colon). Mistmatch caused the policy engine to treat some tenants as eligible for fallthrough and a separate header-rewrite path in the runtime rewrote tenant headers when binding to dedicated pool, resulting in cross-tenant mapping for ~3% of requests during the burst.

carla (runtime): adding more detail: the header-rewrite was intended to annotate routed requests with pool metadata. Bug: when a tenant namespace is missing, we fallback to the first available namespace and write that header — that's what caused the exposure. Fix: change rewrite to skip if namespace missing. I will open PR with tests.

linh (platform): I'll revert the tagging change in infra to remove the ambiguous selector and add stricter unit tests in the policy engine.

maya (eng-oncall): severity: S2 for now (partial customer impact, some timeouts and slow requests, no confirmed data exfil). Support: send outbound to acct-omega with status update and that we're mitigating. Sam can you send a templated note?

sam (support): drafting now. will send 'we observed degraded responses for X timeframe, mitigation applied, next update in 1 hour' and offer incident call if they request.

alice (ops-automation): handing to follow-up owner: carla (runtime) to lead fix PR + alex (sre) to run postmortem. Oncall handoff note: maya will be primary for next 30 mins, then pass to alex for verification and timeline.

maya (eng-oncall): confirmed. leaving monitoring in place. if we see reoccurrence alert @carla and @alex.

carla (runtime): PR opened: https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/482. tests added for header-rewrite skip. I'll schedule a canary deploy to prod when approved.

alex (sre): creating incident stub and postmortem placeholder: https://redwood-incidents/INC-8942/postmortem. Adding timeline and metrics.

maya (eng-oncall): thanks team. closing immediate emergency. continuing watch for 1 hour.

incident-bot: Incident unpaged, status: mitigated. PD INC-8942 set to "acknowledged -> resolved" after verification window.

carla (runtime): follow-ups: 1) fix header-rewrite logic (PR) 2) tighten policy selector syntax and add lint check 3) run replay of routing logs for last 7d to confirm no prior occurrences 4) add post-deploy smoke that validates tenant isolation.

alex (sre): I'll include the long-term fix items in the postmortem. Thanks all for fast response.

sam (support): outbound update sent to impacted customers.

maya (eng-oncall): incident thread archived in 1hr unless new alerts. Closing channel updates for now.
